clue.text: German movement endlessly quiet, after jail term

indicators.note: after places the shortened word for quiet behind the jail and term pieces

parts.note: jug is slang for a prison
an end is a term or limit

indicators.note: endlessly says the last letter of the word for quiet is dropped

parts.note: still means quiet

explanation.surface: A German political movement goes silent once its leaders have served time in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the final letter of the quiet word; 'after' puts the result behind the jail and term pieces. 'German movement' suggests politics, but it is an art style.
explanation.definitionFit: Jugendstil was the German art nouveau style, an artistic movement of around 1900.

clue.text: Tool needed to lift aircraft

parts.note: to jack is to lift, as with a car jack
a plane is an aircraft

explanation.surface: Equipment is required to raise an aeroplane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aircraft' points to an aeroplane, but the answer is a carpenter's plane.
explanation.definitionFit: A jack plane is a general-purpose woodworking plane for rough shaping, a carpenter's tool.

clue.text: I broke into allowance to get a type of AIS N sorbet

annotationWithheld.clue: I broke into allowance to get a type of AIS N sorbet

clue.text: Swimmer, rather hard of hearing, seen across lake

indicators.note: seen across says the word for somewhat deaf spans, or is laid across, the lake letter

parts.note: deafish means somewhat deaf
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A slightly deaf swimmer is spotted crossing a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen across' puts DEAFISH around L. 'Swimmer' looks like a person but is a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The dealfish is a long, ribbon-like deep-sea fish, so a swimmer in crossword terms.

clue.text: Somewhat deficient case of wine available for a song?

definitions.text: Somewhat deficient case of wine available for a song?

parts.words: Somewhat deficient case of wine available for a song?
parts.note: a full case of wine holds a dozen; one a couple short would be a cheap bargain, but also the number in a well-known counting-down children's song about bottles on a wall

explanation.surface: A wine case missing a couple of bottles is going cheap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a song' means cheaply, but also points to the British children's counting song in which bottles fall one by one off a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A case of twelve less two leaves this many; it is also the title of a popular counting-down children's song.

clue.text: Messenger's extremely louche entrance

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so messenger is the definition

indicators.note: extremely picks the letters at the very extremes of the word louche

parts.note: a gate is an entrance

explanation.surface: An envoy makes a decidedly disreputable entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes the first and last letters of LOUCHE, L and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A legate is an envoy or emissary, especially one representing the Pope.

clue.text: Wrath perhaps shown by head

definitions.meaning: ... Wrath is a headland at the far north-west tip of Scotland, one example of such a promontory
a head is a headland, a promontory jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: Someone's anger shows on their face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrath' reads as anger, but it is the Scottish headland Cape Wrath.
explanation.definitionFit: A headland jutting into the sea is called both a head and a cape; Wrath is one in Scotland.

clue.text: Several countries maybe exercising self-restraint

definitions.meaning: a large land mass such as Europe or Africa, made up of many nations
showing control over one's appetites or bodily functions

explanation.surface: Several nations may be practising moderation.
explanation.definitionFit: A continent is a landmass of many countries; continent as an adjective means self-restrained.

clue.text: Quietly rave about Greek character, an upstart

parts.note: P is piano, the musical term for quietly

indicators.note: about suggests the letters of rave are turned around and jumbled

parts.note: nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone quietly enthuses about a Greek figure who is a social climber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' jumbles the four letters of rave, giving ARVE, which sits between the piano mark and the Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A parvenu is someone newly risen to wealth or status, an upstart.

clue.text: Tea taken with simple man of God

parts.note: cha is an informal British word for tea
plain means simple

explanation.surface: A clergyman has a cup of tea with a plain meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplain is a clergyman attached to an institution, so a man of God.

clue.text: Endlessly get at New Age types

indicators.note: endlessly says the word get loses its final letter

parts.note: an era is an age

explanation.surface: Someone keeps nagging at New Age followers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' trims GET to GE; 'at' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Genera are classes or kinds, the plural of genus, so types.

clue.text: Sound of bubbly in mug

indicators.note: sound of says the word for bubbly is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: fizz is a colloquial word for champagne, bubbly

explanation.surface: Champagne makes a noise as it is poured into a cup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mug' looks like a drinking vessel for the bubbly, but it is slang for the face.
explanation.definitionFit: Phiz is old slang for the face, short for physiognomy, and mug is slang for the face too.

clue.text: Emergency worker making tree more steady

parts.note: a fir is a coniferous tree
staider means more sedate, steadier

explanation.surface: A rescuer props up a tree to stop it wobbling.
explanation.definitionFit: A first-aider gives emergency treatment before medical help arrives.

clue.text: Blast area to be exploited for mineral

indicators.note: exploited suggests the words are worked over and reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An area is to be blasted so it can be mined for a mineral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be exploited' rearranges the letters of BLAST AREA.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabaster is a fine-grained form of gypsum or calcite, a mineral used in carving.

clue.text: Programme of entertainment introduced by coarse singer

indicators.note: introduced by puts the coarse piece in front of the programme

parts.note: broad humour is coarse or vulgar
a bill is a list of acts in a show, as in top of the bill

explanation.surface: A music-hall programme is opened by a crude vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'singer' looks like a performer on the bill, but it is a songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: The broadbill is a tropical perching bird, and crosswords often call any bird a singer.

clue.text: Relaxation permitted at university

parts.note: let means allowed or permitted
up means in residence at university, as in being up at Oxford

explanation.surface: Being allowed to go to university brings some relief.
explanation.definitionFit: A let-up is a pause or easing off, a relaxation of effort or pressure.

clue.text: Use subtle humour in caustic way

definitions.meaning: read as two words, to make a play on words softly or delicately
sharply or bitingly, as of a remark or smell

explanation.surface: Wit is used delicately in a sharp manner.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the answer into PUN (use humour) and GENTLY (subtly).
explanation.definitionFit: Pungent means sharp or biting, so a caustic remark is made in that manner.

clue.text: Doubtful at first, subsequently church upheld papal edict

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of the word doubtful
upheld in a down clue means held upwards, so the words are read from bottom to top

parts.note: later means subsequently
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A papal decree, doubted at first, is later upheld by the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upheld' reads the later-plus-church pair from bottom to top in this down entry, giving ECRETAL after the opening D.
explanation.definitionFit: A decretal is a papal decree, especially one settling a point of church law.

clue.text: Drunk topes in bar

indicators.note: drunk suggests the word topes is staggering about, so its letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Someone tipples in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' rearranges TOPES (topes means drinks heavily). 'bar' looks like a pub but is a legal verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To estop is a legal term meaning to bar or preclude someone from asserting something.

clue.text: Dog, female, left on leash

parts.note: she is the female pronoun
a tie is a cord or leash for tethering

explanation.surface: A bitch has been left on her lead.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheltie is a Shetland sheepdog, a small herding dog breed.

clue.text: I aim at first to get on, but …

indicators.note: at first says the word for aim comes before the I

parts.note: an object is an aim or goal
taken as written

explanation.surface: An unfinished sentence: I mean, first, to get on, but then something interrupts.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on to 22-across. 'but' is a noun here, as in 'no ifs or buts', an objection.
explanation.definitionFit: A but is an objection or reservation, as in the phrase 'no buts'.

clue.text: What Liberace played, displaying teeth

definitions.meaning: Liberace was a flamboyant American pianist, and piano keys are made of ivory
slang for teeth, which resemble ivory

explanation.surface: The flamboyant pianist shows off his grin.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivories is slang for piano keys and also for teeth, both white like ivory.

clue.text: Sort of palest colour

indicators.note: sort here means to sort out, so the letters of palest are rearranged

explanation.surface: A kind of very light colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' rearranges the letters of PALEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastel is a pale, soft shade of colour.

clue.text: … teacher has rated me falsely

indicators.note: falsely suggests the words are wrongly arranged, so their letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Continuing from 19-across: an objection that the head teacher has marked someone unfairly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falsely' rearranges the letters of HAS RATED ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A headmaster is the male head teacher of a school.

clue.text: Heartless sheriff's team in position

indicators.note: heartless says the central letter of the word for the sheriff's team is removed

parts.note: a posse is a group of men summoned by a sheriff

explanation.surface: A sheriff's band of deputies sits in place without compassion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' takes the middle S out of POSSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pose is a position or posture held, for a portrait for example.

clue.text: My specialist subject may be Ovid: can I enter final?

definitions.text: My specialist subject may be Ovid

indicators.note: enter says the can and the I go inside the word for final

parts.note: last means final
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A quiz contestant hopes to reach the final with the Roman poet Ovid as their chosen topic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enter' puts the can and the I inside the word for final. The definition is spoken by the answer itself: Ovid wrote in Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latinist is a scholar of Latin, whose subject would include the poet Ovid.

clue.text: Cruel man ignoring cry of pain

indicators.note: ignoring says the cry of pain is left out of the word for man

parts.note: a fellow is a man
ow is an exclamation of pain

explanation.surface: A brutal man pays no attention to someone's yelp of pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring' removes OW from FELLOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Fell is an old adjective meaning fierce or cruel, as in 'one fell swoop'.

clue.text: Ko-Ko didn't perform his song so unenthusiastically

definitions.text: Ko-Ko didn't perform his song so
definitions.meaning: Ko-Ko in Gilbert and Sullivan's The Mikado sings 'I've got a little list', so without it he would be minus his list

explanation.surface: An operetta character skips his number with a shrug.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the answer as without-list, in the manner of Ko-Ko omitting his famous list song.
explanation.definitionFit: Listless means lacking energy or enthusiasm, so doing something in that manner is half-hearted.
